# AI Engineering Compiler v0.6.2

A documentation release. Nothing the compiler generates changes, so there is
nothing to re-sync.

## An upgrade guide

[`docs/upgrading.md`](https://github.com/akin-oz/ai-engineering/blob/v0.6.2/docs/upgrading.md)
collects what changed since 0.2.0 by what a project uses:

- **Everyone:** install the latest version, run `aie sync`, and replace `ai`
  with `aie`.
- **Turning on `security: hardened`:** what it adds, accepting the Codex or
  Cursor gap, pre-allowing network hosts, and what happens to an existing
  `settings.json`.
- **Checking the result** with `aie audit`.
- **GitHub Action users:** the audit already runs in warn mode on `v0`, and
  `audit: fail` makes it fail the job.
- **Blueprint users:** the hardened commit guard, the `protect-guardrails` deny
  rules, the CI trailer check, and how to turn each off.
- **A table of what each release changed**, 0.3.0 through 0.6.1.

It also says plainly where the sandbox's shell protections stop: on native
Windows, when the sandbox cannot start, and on an approved retry outside it.

The README links the guide under the quick start. The docs test checks that
every diagnostic code the guide names still exists.
